scenario.name: Red Hat Security, CNCF Tetragon & MITRE — Container CAP_SYS_MODULE Host Kernel Module (finit_module) Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a bustling coastal shipping port with blue harbor water, stacked colorful steel cargo containers, a towering yellow overhead gantry crane, and a moored cargo ship. Out on the concrete harbor pier, a worker notices a single shipping container whose side inspection hatch was accidentally left unlatched during loading. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the harbor crane inspection pier in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the harbor crane inspection pier in tiny disguised batches. The port authority watchtower spots footsteps leaving a supposedly sealed container bay and compares the manifest seal numbers against the pier camera. In this scenario (T1082, Red Hat Security, CNCF Tetragon & MITRE, Container CAP_SYS_MODULE Host Kernel Module , finit_module Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: inspecting /proc/self/status CapEff Bit 16, then invoking finit_module / init_module, then host Kernel /proc/modules Taint Flag. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Inspecting /proc/self/status CapEff Bit 16, then Invoking finit_module / init_module, then Host Kernel /proc/modules Taint Flag, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1082 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Inspecting /proc/self/status CapEff Bit 16 (CAP_SYS_MODULE) & Host uname -r
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1082 - System Information Discovery)
stages.description: Out on the concrete harbor pier, a worker notices a single shipping container whose side inspection hatch was accidentally left unlatched during loading. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the harbor crane inspection pier in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the harbor customs inspector go about their routine. Because all containers on a Linux node share the same host kernel, a container process checks /proc/self/status for CapEff bit 16 (0x0000000000010000 = CAP_SYS_MODULE) and runs uname -r to match the host kernel ABI version (logged in Linux Audit Event 63 with DetectedCapability=CAP_SYS_MODULE , Bit 16, PodIdentity=default/legacy-net-agent, SensorSource=Cilium Tetragon eBPF so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes capsh --decode=00000000a80525fb (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , capsh --decode=00000000a80525fb configuring pod security contexts, volume mounts so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1082 during "Inspecting /proc/self/status CapEff Bit 16 , CAP_SYS_MODULE & Host uname -r" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact uname -r && cat /proc/version runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , uname -r && cat /proc/version via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact ar so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1082 during "Inspecting /proc/self/status CapEff Bit 16 , CAP_SYS_MODULE & Host uname -r" , Because all containers on a Linux node share the same host kernel, a container process checks /proc/self/status for CapEff bit 16 , 0x0000000000010000 = CAP_SYS_MODULE and runs uname -r to match the host kernel ABI version while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.title: Stage 2: Invoking finit_module (Syscall 313) / init_module (Syscall 175) via insmod
stages.subtitle: Escape to Host & Persistence (T1547.006 - Kernel Modules and Extensions)
stages.description: Slipping out through that open container hatch while the yellow gantry crane swings overhead, the stowaway steps straight onto the restricted customs dockyard. Here in Step 2 inside the shipping port, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the harbor crane inspection pier in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the sealed bonded export yard. keySpecs.value: Enable kernel.modules_disabled=1 via sysctl on immutable Kubernetes worker nodes after boot, enforce CONFIG_MODULE_SIG_FORCE=y (signed kernel modules only), and block init_module/finit_module in the container Seccomp profile.
